proposition: Without ranking from filenames, what do inventoried permit documents establish, and which document governs if they disagree?
would_establish: Issued final_permit cover pages self-define the binding permit corpus as named Parts I–III/IV and internally cross-referenced appendices.
Supporting fact_sheet and statement_of_basis texts frame content as draft/proposed rationale and defer enforceable limitations to the permit document.
Reasonable_potential files function as calculation appendices subordinate to fact sheets, not standalone authorization.
Part_ii_appendix and part_iv files are incorporated into the governing corpus when the issued final_permit cross-references them.
Filename document_kind labels are not a reliable hierarchy signal for authority or conflict precedence.
would_refute: document_inventory.json document_kind ordering (final_permit > fact_sheet > reasonable_potential) determines both content authority and conflict precedence.
All twelve inventoried files are independently binding authorizations with no functional precedence among them.
Precedence is unknowable unless an explicit 'in the event of conflict' clause appears between package documents.
insufficient_alone: sources/document_inventory.json alone cannot establish authority or precedence because it lists kinds, filenames, and hashes only.
documents/INDEX.md alone is a byte inventory without narrative text.
Any single supporting document (fact_sheet, statement_of_basis, reasonable_potential) cannot establish a global precedence rule across all twelve files.
Absence of an explicit inter-document conflict clause does not, by itself, prove that no functional precedence exists.
